Refactoring to introduce proper ports and adapters will restore layer boundaries and improve maintainability.

rationales.why_it_matters: Application code imports the Presentation layer, violating the rule that inner layers must not depend on outer layers, leading to tight coupling and brittle startup code.
rationales.prescribed_fix: Define an Application‑level port (e.g., IAppEntry) that abstracts the entry point, implement it in the Presentation layer, and inject the implementation into main via Dependency Injection.

rationales.why_it_matters: The Application layer directly references Infrastructure, breaking the inward‑only dependency direction and entangling business start‑up logic with persistence details.
rationales.prescribed_fix: Create a Repository port (e.g., IDatabaseInitializer) in the Application layer, implement it in infrastructure.database, and inject the adapter into main.

rationales.why_it_matters: Domain logic reaches into Infrastructure, contaminating pure business rules with I/O concerns and preventing isolated testing.
rationales.prescribed_fix: Introduce a FraudRepository port inside the Domain layer, implement the concrete DatabaseConnection adapter in infrastructure.database, and inject the repository into domain.fraud_checker.

rationales.why_it_matters: Domain code depends on Presentation controllers, inverting the intended flow and coupling core business rules to UI formatting.
rationales.prescribed_fix: Remove the import; expose a plain Result object from the Domain and let the Presentation controller format the response after invoking the Domain use‑case.

rationales.why_it_matters: Infrastructure adapters reference Presentation middleware, causing delivery‑layer leakage into low‑level services and tying logging to HTTP context.
rationales.prescribed_fix: Define an AuditLogger port (e.g., IAuditLogger) in the Application or Domain layer, implement it in infrastructure.audit_logger, and pass user context as method parameters from the Application layer.

rationales.why_it_matters: Presentation directly accesses the database, bypassing Application use‑cases and coupling the web layer to persistence details.
rationales.prescribed_fix: Create an OrderService port in the Application layer, implement the service using a Repository adapter in infrastructure.database, and have presentation.order_routes call the service instead of importing the database directly.

roadmap: Refactor main to depend on an Application‑level port for the Presentation API (IAppEntry) and inject the concrete implementation.
Introduce an Application‑level repository port (IDatabaseInitializer) for database bootstrapping and inject the infrastructure adapter into main.
Add a FraudRepository port in the Domain layer; implement it in infrastructure.database and inject into domain.fraud_checker.
Remove the import of presentation.controllers from domain.payment_rule; let Presentation format results after calling the Domain use‑case.
Create an IAuditLogger port in Application/Domain, implement it in infrastructure.audit_logger, and pass authentication context from the Application layer.

Introduce an OrderService use‑case port in Application, implement it with a repository adapter in infrastructure.database, and have presentation.order_routes call this service instead of importing the database.

audit_narrative.summary: The ecommerce_platform codebase scores 60% health and exhibits six major architectural violations. All violations stem from layers depending outward, breaking the clean‑architecture rule that dependencies must point inward. Refactoring to introduce proper ports and adapters will restore layer boundaries and improve maintainability.

rationales.why_it_matters: Application code imports the Presentation layer, violating the rule that inner layers must not depend on outer layers, leading to tight coupling and brittle startup code.
rationales.prescribed_fix: Define an Application‑level port (e.g., IAppEntry) that abstracts the entry point, implement it in the Presentation layer, and inject the implementation into main via Dependency Injection.

rationales.why_it_matters: The Application layer directly references Infrastructure, breaking the inward‑only dependency direction and entangling business start‑up logic with persistence details.
rationales.prescribed_fix: Create a Repository port (e.g., IDatabaseInitializer) in the Application layer, implement it in infrastructure.database, and inject the adapter into main.

rationales.why_it_matters: Domain logic reaches into Infrastructure, contaminating pure business rules with I/O concerns and preventing isolated testing.
rationales.prescribed_fix: Introduce a FraudRepository port inside the Domain layer, implement the concrete DatabaseConnection adapter in infrastructure.database, and inject the repository into domain.fraud_checker.

rationales.why_it_matters: Domain code depends on Presentation controllers, inverting the intended flow and coupling core business rules to UI formatting.
rationales.prescribed_fix: Remove the import; expose a plain Result object from the Domain and let the Presentation controller format the response after invoking the Domain use‑case.

rationales.why_it_matters: Infrastructure adapters reference Presentation middleware, causing delivery‑layer leakage into low‑level services and tying logging to HTTP context.
rationales.prescribed_fix: Define an AuditLogger port (e.g., IAuditLogger) in the Application or Domain layer, implement it in infrastructure.audit_logger, and pass user context as method parameters from the Application layer.

rationales.why_it_matters: Presentation directly accesses the database, bypassing Application use‑cases and coupling the web layer to persistence details.
rationales.prescribed_fix: Create an OrderService port in the Application layer, implement the service using a Repository adapter in infrastructure.database, and have presentation.order_routes call the service instead of importing the database directly.

roadmap: Refactor main to depend on an Application‑level port for the Presentation API (IAppEntry) and inject the concrete implementation.
Introduce an Application‑level repository port (IDatabaseInitializer) for database bootstrapping and inject the infrastructure adapter into main.
Add a FraudRepository port in the Domain layer; implement it in infrastructure.database and inject into domain.fraud_checker.
Remove the import of presentation.controllers from domain.payment_rule; let Presentation format results after calling the Domain use‑case.
Create an IAuditLogger port in Application/Domain, implement it in infrastructure.audit_logger, and pass authentication context from the Application layer.

Introduce an OrderService use‑case port in Application, implement it with a repository adapter in infrastructure.database, and have presentation.order_routes call this service instead of importing the database.
